**D5 — Hub-only git carve-out. Claudy runs git in the Hub; Tony alone creates the PR and merges.** Inside this family, for DocSet synchronization in the Doctrine Hub only: Claudy may create and work on the approved sync branch, commit approved synchronization changes, and push ONLY at the authorized push boundary (D18). Tony creates the PR from the compare URL, reviews, and merges (rebase-and-merge for doctrine work; squash only for trivia). Tony is never asked to run git. **Provenance and limits of this exception:** it is the Operator's standing ruling for the documentation Hub (2026-08-05, reconfirmed in Stage B Ruling 2, 2026-09-14). It is a bounded exception for a docs-only repository with branch protection on main. It does NOT redefine the Engineer git-zero / cloud-zero doctrine that governs BIM, FIX, FEAT, TRM, and all application-module work (`BIM_PLAYBOOK` §2/§7, `BUG_FIX_PLAYBOOK` §3), where the Coordinator commits and the Engineer stages nothing. A future agent reading this rule must not generalize it. Rationale for the exception: hand-driven git produced three recovery incidents in one day (a rejected main push, a stash tangle, a `reset --hard` file loss); the Operator's time belongs at the decision gates. Rationale for rebase-and-merge: it preserves one-commit-per-doc history, which is what makes `git log --follow` on a doctrine file a readable audit trail.

**D6 — Main is PR-only. Absolute.** Never write to main; never call `merge_pull_request`; every run's changes live on a run branch that starts at the approved BASE_SHA (D18), never on main. On main you PULL, never push. Branch protection enforces this as physics. This is the one rule no in-session override can waive (§6).

**D9 — Lint conduct and baseline.** The Hub's four lints run in CI on every push and PR. Run them locally BEFORE every commit (shift-left; a fixup commit on 2026-08-05 bought this). A failure CAUSED by your change is fixed before the commit. A PRE-EXISTING failure is recorded in the baseline at discovery, reported, never fixed uninvited, and NEVER exempted — adding exempt-patterns to make CI green blinds the drift-killer (AP-5). The baseline (count + paths) travels in the UPDATE MAP §M and the handoff; QA proves it unchanged.

**D10 — Writable surface, per seat.** *Claudy:* canonical writes (after Gate 2, D2) — files on the approved touch list, approved new canonical files, `MANIFEST.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` per the approved map, `_ARCHIVE/` (additions only), `_INBOX/` (dispositioning cargo out of it at sweep); run-state / planning writes (any phase) — the run's durable folder `_AUDIT/SYNC_<date>_<slug>/` (including the immutable `INTAKE_SNAPSHOT/` copied at Gate 1), `RECOVERY.md`, the session file, and `agent_docs/RESPONSES/` per the repo protocol. *Sol:* the acceptance spec (until frozen at Gate 3) and `GATE_Q_REPORT.md` in the durable folder, `RECOVERY.md`, the session file. *Cody:* `QA_MATRIX.md` and findings in the durable folder, the session file. Everything else in the Hub — every other tier doc, other `_SKILLS/*`, `lints/`, `.github/`, `_OTHERS/`, the approved map after Gate 2 (Claudy may amend it only through a Gate 2 re-approval — no other post-freeze write, not even CONTENT_SHA or the Gate 4 time: those live in `SYNC_HANDOFF.md` / `RUN_SUMMARY.md`, D18), the spec after Gate 3, and `INTAKE_SNAPSHOT/` after Gate 1 — is read-only for every seat. Nobody "fixes things noticed along the way"; they go under CONCERNS or become follow-up findings.

**D11 — Close-out sweep, durable versus debris.** No job ends with floating files. **Durable** (survives the campaign, rides the PR): the run's `_AUDIT/SYNC_<date>_<slug>/` folder — `UPDATE_MAP.md` (with approval and amendment log), `DOCSET_SYNC_ACCEPTANCE_SPEC.md` (LARGE), `SYNC_HANDOFF.md`, `QA_MATRIX.md` and findings (LARGE), `GATE_Q_REPORT.md` (LARGE), **`INTAKE_SNAPSHOT/`** — every in-scope cargo unit copied byte-for-byte as received, at Gate 1, never edited afterwards (or, only when a unit is too large to snapshot, `INTAKE_SNAPSHOT/REFERENCE.md` naming its immutable source: repository, commit SHA, path) — and `RUN_SUMMARY.md` (which carries CONTENT_SHA, the Gate 4 record, the pushed tip, and the final per-ID disposition stamps). On LARGE the snapshot MUST be committed no later than the handoff commit so that it rides the Gate 4 push: TEST B (2026-09) proved a fresh QA worktree had the pushed map, spec, and handoff but not the Engineer's local, uncommitted `_INBOX/` — Cody must never depend on it. On the TINY path the durable set is `UPDATE_MAP.md` (with the waiver line), `INTAKE_SNAPSHOT/`, and `RUN_SUMMARY.md` (with CONTENT_SHA). **Debris** (removed before Gate Q closeout on LARGE, before the sweep ends on TINY): per-cycle scratch files and grep dumps; duplicates of durable artifacts elsewhere (RESPONSES copies are dispositioned per the Operator's standing 2026-08-10 ruling — deletions are a NAMED housekeeping commit, never a passenger in a doctrine commit); abandoned local or remote branches; `_INBOX/` contents (every unit landed, parked, or returned — the bay stays, empty); stray `__pycache__`; editor backups. Session files and `RECOVERY.md` stay at the repo root per repo protocol. Three separate incidents (a stash dance, a vanished recon report, session-file drift) bought this rule; 71 orphaned response logs bought the debris half.

**D15a — Evidence-driven resume, any seat, any phase.** **Recovery authority hierarchy.** `RECOVERY.md` and the session files are ADVISORY state: convenient, often right, never authoritative. Authoritative recovery evidence is, in this order: the git branch, HEAD, and history; the working-tree diff (`git status --porcelain`, `git diff`); the `_AUDIT/SYNC_*` artifacts and their status lines; the approved UPDATE MAP; the intake and its durable `INTAKE_SNAPSHOT/`; and canonical disk reality. If RECOVERY / session state is stale, missing, or contradicts any of these, git + disk + the approved durable artifacts win, and the discrepancy is reported, not reconciled silently. A fresh agent with no conversational memory and no graceful shutdown behind it must be able to reconstruct from that evidence alone: the active run, BASE_SHA, the approved route, the status of every gate, the current phase, the EXPECTED dirty state, and the next legal action (TEST C2, hard-crash resume, 2026-09). On a declared or detected RESUME: (1) read `RECOVERY.md` and the session file for the claimed state — if absent, skip them; (2) verify against reality — `git branch -a`, `git log` on candidate branches, `git status`, `_INBOX/`, `_ARCHIVE/` additions, the durable folder's contents and their status lines; disk and git win over recovery prose; (2a) **classify the dirty set:** compare every uncommitted path against the run's approved expected run-state set (UPDATE MAP §N — the map itself, `INTAKE_SNAPSHOT/`, session / recovery state, response logs, the draft RUN_SUMMARY); a dirty set that is exactly a subset of that approved set is a LAWFUL interrupted-run state, not a STOP (TEST C1); any unexplained path → STOP / BLOCKED → Tony; (3) locate the phase from the durable folder: no map → P1; map DRAFT → P2; map APPROVED and no spec (LARGE) → P3; spec APPROVED and commits but no handoff → P4 (inventory DONE / NOT DONE per touch-list row with evidence); handoff present and not pushed → Gate 4; pushed and no matrix → P6; matrix partial → P6 at the last recorded row; findings routed → rework; Gate Q verdict present → P8/P9; (4) re-present from the last COMPLETED gate; a half-executed phase is re-presented for its remaining rows, not re-argued from scope; (5) a half-done branch is adopted or cleanly abandoned by the Operator's explicit word, never both, never silently. **QA resume:** a resumed Cody session re-verifies `QA_START_SHA` (or the latest `QA_RETEST_SHA`) against `origin/<branch>` before trusting any previously recorded PASS row; if the tip moved, every row is re-run. The map — not memory, not the branch — remains the source of truth.

**D20 — QA independence and derivation-only acceptance.** On the LARGE path QA is a separate seat in a separate session. Sol authors `DOCSET_SYNC_ACCEPTANCE_SPEC.md` after Gate 2 under the derivation-only rule: every AC traces to an approved Correction / Intake ID, an approved UPDATE MAP row, or a standing invariant family in `_shared/references/STANDING_INVARIANTS.md`; Sol transforms approved intent into testable criteria and may NOT invent doctrine requirements. Tony approves the spec at Gate 3; it is frozen; any material change re-enters Gate 3. Cody verifies at QA_START_SHA with read-only checks and writes evidence only in QA surfaces; Cody may not edit canonical doctrine, the map, the spec, MANIFEST, CHANGELOG, `_ARCHIVE/`, or branch history, may not rewrite Claudy's wording, and may not adjudicate new doctrine. Sol reviews Cody's evidence, classifies and routes findings, and owns the Gate Q verdict in the Factory vocabulary — PASS / PASS WITH FOLLOW-UP FINDINGS / PASS WITH KNOWN RISK / FAIL / BLOCKED — and no other. Claudy never issues a verdict and never grades his own paper on LARGE. On the TINY path, the docs-only QA waiver (`SOFTWARE_FACTORY_PLAYBOOK` §2.5 item 6) is recorded explicitly in the map at Gate 2, and Claudy runs the mechanical checks of the standing invariants himself and presents them at Gate 4. Rationale: `QA_PLAYBOOK` §34 names Engineer self-certification an anti-pattern; §3 forbids QA silently repairing what it verifies; `BIM_PLAYBOOK` §8 forbids the Engineer writing his own exam.

A **cargo unit** is one file, or one folder treated as a whole, in `_INBOX/` (legacy fallback: the repo root for `DOCTRINE_PROMOTION*`, `*PATCH*`, `LESSONS*`). A correction package arrives as a folder tree and is ONE unit at the package level; each correction inside it is one ledger ROW. Recognition is by discovery, never by asking Tony what a file is, and it is **content-first**. Read the unit and decide from its **status** (APPROVED, FLAGGED, DRAFT, historical), **contents**, **intent** (what it asks to become true), **target** (which doc, repo, or folder it aims at), **provenance** (who produced it, from which run or retro), **authority** (who approved it, and whether that approval governs doctrine), and **semantic form** (brief, entry, whole document, image, record), plus a Hub-counterpart match by canonical name first and content similarity second. The **filename is supporting evidence only**: a file is not a lesson because "LESSONS" is in its name, and a file named otherwise is not excluded from a class its contents prove. When filename and contents disagree, contents win and the disagreement is stated aloud.
